diagnostic_evidence.quote: For each subset of indices $T \subseteq \set{1, \ldots, \omega}$, define $n_T = N\sum_{t \in T} \frac{1}{p_t}$.
Note that this construction is well defined.

issues.failure_explanation: The construction assigns entries at indices n_T without reducing modulo N. For N=30 and T={2,3,5}, n_T=30(1/2+1/3+1/5)=31, which is not a valid index of a length-30 signal. The proof only shows n_T1 != n_T2 as integers, not that the indices lie in {0,...,N-1}. Thus the stated construction is ill-defined for general N.

failure_location.quote: For every possible value of $n_T$, let $x_{n_T} = (-1)^{\abs{T}}$,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the support modulo N (e.g. x_{n_T mod N}) and prove that the residues n_T mod N remain distinct, or give another valid {-1,0,1} construction.
issues.overall_effect: The lower-bound ambiguity construction, and therefore the 2D lower-bound results that use it, are unsupported for lengths with at least three distinct prime factors, including N=30 used in the paper's examples.
issues.title: 1D ambiguity construction uses indices that can exceed N-1
issues.why_classification: The fix is local to the construction and preserves the lemma, but it requires a nontrivial well-definedness argument beyond a one-line typo repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, set $m_j = j(k/d_1)^{-1}p \bmod{N_1}$ for the row index,

issues.failure_explanation: If d1=gcd(k,N1)>1, k/d1 need not be invertible modulo N1. For example, N1=12, k=8, d1=4 gives k/d1=2, which is not invertible modulo 12. The Bezout construction of m_j and n_j therefore fails as written.

failure_location.quote: Since $d_1 = \gcd(k, N_1)$ and $d_2 = \gcd(l, N_2)$, $k/d_1$ and $l/d_2$ must have multiplicative inverses modulo $N_1$ and $N_2$, respectively.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use inverses modulo D1=N1/d1 and D2=N2/d2, then lift the resulting congruences to indices modulo N1 and N2.
issues.overall_effect: The proof that each subsignal entry sums exactly M=N1N2/D matrix entries is incomplete, weakening the construction used in the 2D ambiguity lemma and lower bound.
issues.title: Subsignal proof assumes false inverses modulo N1 and N2
issues.why_classification: A short local correction to the moduli repairs the proof without changing the lemma's statement or downstream conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let ${\bf x}$ be the signal of length $D$ defined in \Cref{lem:amb1D}.

issues.failure_explanation: The embedded 1D signal has length D, so lem:amb1D gives nonzero DFT coefficients exactly when gcd(lambda,D)=1. The proof instead asserts gcd(lambda,N)=1. Since D can be a proper divisor of N, the proof misses equivalent frequencies whose lambda is coprime to D but not to N.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by gcd(lambda,D)=1 (and include the factor M in the equality if an exact coefficient value is intended).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the 2D ambiguity lemma does not establish the claimed nonzero pattern on the full equivalence class whenever D<N.
issues.title: 2D ambiguity proof tests gcd(lambda,N) instead of gcd(lambda,D)
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of the wrong modulus in a proof step; the lemma's intended statement survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed general formula is false. For N1=N2=4 it gives 11, but Z4 x Z4 has only 10 cyclic subgroups; the source's own prime-power specialization with p=2, alpha=2 gives 10. Thus the claimed general counting formula contradicts the correct special cases and the actual group structure.

failure_location.quote: c(N_1, N_2) = \sum_{a\divs N_1, b\divs N_2} \phi(\gcd(a, b)),

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:n_subgroups with a correct formula for the number of cyclic subgroups of Z_N1 x Z_N2 and correct the derivation of the special cases; at minimum, remove the false general expression.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's stated general method for computing the minimal number of DFT coefficients from the cyclic-subgroup count is unreliable, although the conceptual corollary that the number equals the number of cyclic subgroups remains correct.
issues.title: False general formula for number of cyclic subgroups
issues.why_classification: The correction is contained to the counting section, but it requires supplying a correct nontrivial counting formula rather than a one-line fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \Require a representative DFT coefficient $\tilde{X}_{k, l}$ for each coefficient class

issues.failure_explanation: Invert1D requires divisor-indexed coefficients for the subsignal, not merely an unordered set of values. Moreover, for non-unit divisors lambda of D, the frequency (lambda k, lambda l) lies in a smaller 2D coefficient class. The algorithm only initially knows one representative per class and specifies no order ensuring the needed smaller-class coefficients have been recovered and that the specific frequency is filled in.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify a topological order (e.g. increasing D) and pass an explicitly divisor-labelled set of already recovered coefficients, or replace the call by the ordered memoized procedure.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the high-level 2D procedure is not well-defined and may call Invert1D with unavailable or improperly labelled data.
issues.title: High-level 2D algorithm passes an unordered, unlabelled coefficient set to Invert1D
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local specification of ordering and input labelling; it does not change the underlying mathematical reduction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We multiply the entire basis ${\tt B}$ by $\beta_3$ and then truncate the scaled basis, before passing $\lfloor\beta_3{\tt B}\rfloor$ to the FPLLL algorithm.

issues.failure_explanation: The lattice basis is scaled and truncated, so the recovered vector's last coordinate is only an approximation to ±β0. The pseudocode nevertheless uses exact equality b_N = ±β0, which can fail for the correct vector because of the introduced truncation and floating-point reduction errors.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact equality by a tolerance test such as min(|b_N-β0|,|b_N+β0|) ≤ τ for a small τ, consistent with the truncation error.
issues.overall_effect: The stated SVP routine may reject correct shortest vectors, undermining the implemented recovery guarantee.
issues.title: LLL routine tests exact equality b_N = ±β0 after truncation
issues.why_classification: A local change to the acceptance criterion fixes the stated algorithm without altering the lattice construction or analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: These cases require no lattice reduction, since the guess is immediately correct with $\overline{\bf x} = {\bf x}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's 1D uniqueness result uses the τ(N) divisor coefficients. For N=4, τ(4)=3, and for N=6, τ(6)=4; neither requires all N DFT coefficients. The stated justification for skipping lattice reduction in these cases is therefore false.

failure_location.quote: For certain values of $N$, including $N = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6$, unique inversion requires all DFT coefficients.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the list to values with τ(N)=N (or state that the special case applies only when all DFT coefficients are actually supplied).
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm description incorrectly characterizes small-N cases and the reason the initial guess is supposedly exact.
issues.title: False claim that N=4 and N=6 require all DFT coefficients
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and does not affect the main lattice recovery method for general N.
